title: The Stephen Talkhouse
summary: The Amagansett music venue carries the name of Stephen Talkhouse Pharoah, a Montaukett whaler, Civil War veteran and famous walker who died in 1879. Jeremy Dennis’s On This Site photograph of his house site is on view there.
listing_image_alt: The site of Stephen Talkhouse Pharoah’s house, photographed by Jeremy Dennis for On This Site.
why_this_matters: Many people know the Talkhouse as a music venue without knowing whose name it carries. The photograph on view there leads back to Stephen Talkhouse Pharoah’s home and to the Montaukett history behind the name.
introduction_content:
Jeremy Dennis’s Stephen Talkhouse Path (2016), from On This Site, is on view at the Stephen Talkhouse. Dennis photographed the place where Stephen Talkhouse Pharoah lived later in life. The foundation of his house remains there, beside a footpath toward Bridgehampton. Read about the house site.

Stephen Talkhouse Pharoah was born at Molly’s Hill in Springs around 1819–1821. He worked as a whaler, served in the 29th Connecticut Volunteers during the Civil War and was known across the South Fork for walking long distances. He died in 1879 and was buried in Indian Field Cemetery. Read his biography.
whereintheworld_content: The Stephen Talkhouse is at 161 Main Street, Amagansett. It is a bar and music venue, so check its schedule before you go.[1] Visit the venue’s website.
